lockedFacts.label: Classic circuit identity
lockedFacts.value: A loop from Rifugio Auronzo using trails 101 and 105, returning to Rifugio Auronzo.

lockedFacts.label: Approved geometry represents the official circuit
lockedFacts.value: Use the exact 2,077-point official classic GPX approved in export (12).

lockedFacts.label: Official headline metrics
lockedFacts.value: 9.528 km, 468 m ascent, 3 hours 30 minutes, maximum altitude 2,454 m.

lockedFacts.label: Operational trailhead
lockedFacts.value: Rifugio Auronzo, approximately 2,330 m, is the start and finish.

lockedFacts.label: Municipal parking at Rifugio Auronzo
lockedFacts.value: Paid municipal parking serves the Rifugio Auronzo trailhead.

lockedFacts.label: Exact where-to-park GPS pin
lockedFacts.value: Use Parcheggio Rifugio Auronzo (P1), 46.612849, 12.292858, OSM way 1109742730.

lockedFacts.label: Seasonal road and booking conditions
lockedFacts.value: A roughly 6 km paid road from the Misurina area reaches Rifugio Auronzo; operation is seasonal and weather-dependent, parking access is booked, and roadside parking is prohibited.

lockedFacts.label: Dogs and leash conduct
lockedFacts.value: Dogs are accepted on the route; keep them on lead throughout and carry a muzzle for emergencies.

lockedFacts.label: Reliable dog water
lockedFacts.value: A fountain is identified at Malga LangAlm; treat availability and potability as seasonal/unconfirmed.

lockedFacts.label: Shade and heat exposure
lockedFacts.value: Do not rely on tree shade on this high-alpine circuit; carry sun protection and plan the timing conservatively. No shade percentage is claimed.

lockedFacts.label: Technical exposure and surface hazards
lockedFacts.value: No ferrata equipment is required; one section is narrower but described as unchallenging.

lockedFacts.label: Livestock and guardian dogs
lockedFacts.value: Seasonal livestock may be present beside the Lavaredo pasture segment; keep dogs close and on lead. An encounter is not guaranteed and guardian-dog presence is not established.

lockedFacts.label: Publishable trail photograph
lockedFacts.value: Use the geolocated Simone A. Bertinotti Tre Cime route photograph as the initial hero under CC BY-SA 4.0, with full credit, licence link and change notice; retain the operational field-shot checklist for later enrichment.

lockedFacts.label: Assisted route identity
lockedFacts.value: A Bai de Dones loop using the 5 Torri chairlift, Scoiattoli refuge, the open-air museum, Rifugio Cinque Torri and a forest return.

lockedFacts.label: Approved route geometry
lockedFacts.value: Use the exact 204-point official GPX approved in export (12).

lockedFacts.label: Walked ascent and chairlift separation
lockedFacts.value: Treat GPX points 0–22 as 1.37 km of chairlift transport (+295 m raw gain) and points 22–203 as a 3.95 km walk (+10 m/-347 m raw elevation change).

lockedFacts.label: Dogs on the assisted itinerary
lockedFacts.value: Dogs of any size may use the 5 Torri lift free of charge; leash and muzzle are required.

lockedFacts.label: Seasonal lift dependency
lockedFacts.value: The assisted circuit is available only when the 5 Torri chairlift operates; the published 2026 season is 6 June–11 October and remains weather/snow dependent.

lockedFacts.label: Qualitative walking surface
lockedFacts.value: The route mixes museum/trench paths, a cart track and a hiking path through forest; trekking boots are recommended.

lockedFacts.label: Shade and heat exposure
lockedFacts.value: The lower return passes through forest, while the upper museum and refuge area is open alpine terrain; do not rely on continuous shade and do not publish a percentage.

lockedFacts.label: Reliable dog water
lockedFacts.value: Carry water; three refuges offer potential service stops but no freely accessible potable dog-water point is established.

lockedFacts.label: Route POIs
lockedFacts.value: Scoiattoli refuge, the First World War open-air museum and trenches, Rifugio Cinque Torri, Lake Bai de Dones and Baita Bai de Dones are route-linked POIs.

lockedFacts.label: Seasonal livestock caution
lockedFacts.value: Seasonal sheep grazing is documented in the wider Falzarego/Cinque Torri area; keep dogs close and on lead, while treating an encounter on this exact circuit as variable.

lockedFacts.value: Use Clemens Stockner's geolocated Cinque Torri photograph as the initial hero under CC BY-SA 4.0, with full credit, licence link and change notice; retain operational field shots for later enrichment.

lockedFacts.label: Seeweg circuit identity
lockedFacts.value: A complete walking circuit around Lago di Braies, starting and ending at the lake tavern/hotel area.

lockedFacts.label: Approved route geometry
lockedFacts.value: Use the exact 171-point approved GPX.

lockedFacts.label: Headline effort metrics
lockedFacts.value: 3.6 km, 39 m ascent/descent, approximately 1 hour, 1,492–1,531 m elevation.

lockedFacts.label: Official parking choices
lockedFacts.value: Retain the human-approved official P1, P2, P3 and P4 set.

lockedFacts.label: 2026 valley access controls
lockedFacts.value: From 1 July–15 September 2026, 09:00–16:00, enter by public transport, walking, cycling or with a parking reservation/transit permit; shuttle booking is required.

lockedFacts.label: Dogs and transport
lockedFacts.value: The route is dog-friendly; keep dogs on lead in the nature park and carry/use a muzzle on public transport.

lockedFacts.label: Mixed lakeshore surface and narrow sections
lockedFacts.value: The circuit includes broad forest/lakeshore paths plus narrower rooted sections, uphill steps and a section beside a vertical rock wall.

lockedFacts.label: Shade and heat exposure
lockedFacts.value: The circuit mixes tree/forest sections with open lakeshore and southern beaches; do not rely on continuous shade and do not publish a percentage.

lockedFacts.label: Reliable dog water
lockedFacts.value: Carry all water your dog will need. No potable route source is verified, and Lago di Braies must not be presented as a drinking source.

lockedFacts.label: Route POIs and facilities
lockedFacts.value: Boat house, picnic/rest areas, benches, southern beaches, toilets and the lake tavern/hotel area are route-linked facilities and POIs.

lockedFacts.label: Livestock and wildlife interaction
lockedFacts.value: No livestock is expected around the exact Seeweg lakeshore circuit. Keep dogs on lead because protected-area wildlife rules still apply.

lockedFacts.label: Publishable hero asset
lockedFacts.value: Use kallerna's recent geolocated southern-shore photograph as the initial hero under CC BY-SA 4.0, with full credit, licence link and change notice; retain operational field shots for later enrichment.
